subject: Private deployment — access matrix, custodian responsibilities & subprocessors
messages:
From: security@acmemed.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmemed.com, legal@acme.com
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment info request — keys, subprocessors, access boundaries

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking a first pass at this with us. We're evaluating Redwood for a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for parts of our clinical data pipeline and need clarity on a few privacy/operational items before procurement can proceed:

1) Key custody options — can Redwood support: (a) customer-managed keys in our cloud KMS, (b) customer HSM on-prem, and (c) full customer-only key custody with no Redwood access? For each option we'd like a short summary of what operator-level access (if any) is required for day-to-day ops and for incident response.

2) Subprocessors — please provide a current list of subprocessors that would touch private-deploy telemetry or monitoring, plus your policy on notification windows and approval/opt-out. Our legal team will want to understand any third parties in the chain.

3) Data residency / cross-border transfers — we need confirmation of where logs and backups may be stored for VPC vs on-prem; if Redwood routes any telemetry to external services, we need to know locations and safeguards.

4) Operator access and breakglass — what controls and audit trails are in place for emergency operator access? We need JIT, documented approval workflow, and exhaustive audit logs.

Attached is a very high level questionnaire from our security team (we can share a more detailed sheet after your reply). Can you provide a short matrix and sample DPA redlines that show the answers above and proposed language for operator access / subproc clauses?

We'd like to get this clarified over the next two weeks if possible. Proposed timeline: receive materials by June 6, quick sync week of June 9.

Appreciate it —
Sandra Lee
Head of Security
Acme Health Systems
[attachment: acmemed_security_q1.docx]
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: security@acmemed.com
Cc: procurement@acmemed.com, legal@acme.com
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment info request — keys, subprocessors, access boundaries

Sandra — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline and attached a draft access matrix + DPA redline to start the conversation.

Summary answers (high level):
- Key custody: We support the three modes you describe. Customer-managed KMS (cloud) and on-prem HSM give you the strongest guarantees — when configured, Redwood does not hold plaintext model inputs/outputs or keys. We also offer an "operator-assisted" fallback for breakglass which can be designed with JIT policies and customer approval.
- Subprocessors: We keep a short list for monitoring/telemetry and infra (observability, CVM images, managed storage). We notify customers 30 days prior to material changes and can provide a subprocessor attest list; we can discuss longer notice windows in your DPA or carve-outs for regulated workloads.
- Data residency: For VPC deployments we keep control-plane telemetry (aggregated metrics, not raw prompts) in the region you choose; backups are covered by the deployment model — on-prem keeps everything in-customer; VPC backups can be region-locked.
- Operator access / breakglass: JIT access, RBAC, ticketed approvals, and immutable audit logs are standard for private deployments. We can add additional controls (MFA, just-in-time SSH, session recordings) in the deployment SOW.

Attached: access_matrix_v1.xlsx, initial_dpa_redlines_acmemed.pdf (redlines are intentionally conservative).

Looping in Karthik (legal/solutions) and Mina (infrastructure lead) to flesh out the technical constraints and any suggested language changes.

Next steps: Karthik / Mina — can you confirm the specific operator-level telemetry we currently collect for private deployments, and the minimal set we require for safe operations? Also please flag any global subprocessors we should call out for Acme.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[attachment: access_matrix_v1.xlsx][attachment: dpa_redlines_acmemed.pdf]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 31 May 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment info request — keys, subprocessors, access boundaries

Irene / Mina — quick internal note before we reply to Acme. High-level position / proposed language: broken into bullets for clarity.

1) Key custody modes (recommended customer language):
   - Customer-managed KMS (cloud): "Customer holds sole control of encryption keys in their cloud provider KMS. Redwood will not persist plaintext model inputs/outputs nor export keys. Redwood will require an optional, limited encrypted key wrap token to perform instance lifecycle operations; this token is ephemeral and cannot decrypt customer data."
   - On-prem HSM: "Customer maintains keys on a dedicated HSM device; Redwood operators will never have local key material. Operational runbooks will be executed against encrypted artifacts; any operator assistance requires recorded JIT access approved by named customer admins."
   - Exclusive customer custody (no Redwood access): Possible but will increase time to resolve incidents and may restrict certain managed updates. Include an SLA tradeoff clause.

2) Breakglass and operator telemetry (minimum viable telemetry):
   - Minimum telemetry required for safe ops: node health, GPU temperature, process exit codes, encrypted storage mount status, and anonymized failure counters. No raw prompts or embeddings.
   - Breakglass should be: documented ticket, two-person approval (customer + Redwood), time-limited access (max 8 hours), full session recording, and immediate post-incident key rotation option.

3) Subprocesssors & notice windows:
   - Current subprocessors that may see metadata or telemetry: Observability provider (logs aggregation), CI/CD image builder, signed-image storage (S3 provider), and monitoring agent vendor. We can provide a named list under NDA.
   - Proposed contract language: 30 days' notice for new subprocessors + right to object for material changes for regulated customers.

4) Cross-border / residency:
   - For VPCs, control-plane operational logs can remain in the selected region; we should offer a contractual guarantee to persist region locking and prohibit transfer without consent.

5) Next steps for Acme reply:
   - Provide a redlined DPA (attached) and the access_matrix_v1. Ask whether they need a longer subprocessor notice (45/60 days) or explicit approval right. Offer a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Mina to walk the access matrix.

Mina: can you paste the current subprocessors list and confirm the exact telemetry fields we ship for private deployments? I want to make sure we don't accidentally promise less than we currently collect.

—Karthik
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, security@acmemed.com
Cc: procurement@acmemed.com, legal@acme.com
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment info request — access matrix and DPA redlines (consolidated)

Sandra / team — thanks for the clear ask and apologies for the delay. Attaching a concise access matrix and updated DPA redlines (we pared back operator telemetry language per Karthik's notes). Highlights and answers below.

Attachments: access_matrix_v1.xlsx (tabbed per deployment type), dpa_redlines_acmemed.pdf (v2)

Operator access and keys
- Customer-managed KMS (cloud): Supported. When configured correctly, Redwood cannot decrypt customer data without the customer's KMS granting an unwrap. We will not retain key material.
- On-prem HSM: Supported. All operator actions requiring decryption must be performed with customer-provided wrapped keys or via remote attestation; operator assistance requires documented JIT approval.
- Exclusive customer-only custody: Supported but note that emergency incident response will be limited; we recommend an agreed runbook and SLAs for time-to-recover.

Minimal telemetry sent to Redwood-managed endpoints (VPC model only)
- node.health.check (boolean), gpu.metrics (aggregated meta), service.exit.codes (aggregated), encrypted-volume-mount (status), alert.count (anonymized).
- No plaintext prompts, tokens, or embeddings are shipped.

Subprocessors (current list)
- Logs aggregator: Nimbus Observability LLC (aws eu-central region for EU customers)
- Image builder: ForgeCI (build artifacts only; no runtime data)
- Artifact storage: S3-compatible provider (region matched to deployment)
- Monitoring agent vendor: AgentWorks Inc.

Policies & timeline
- Default notice for new subprocessors: 30 days. Regulated customers may request a 60-day notice or a right to object provision (we can negotiate on a case-by-case basis).
- Cross-border: We will region-lock backups and control-plane telemetry per the contract. On-prem deployments keep data in-customer.

Suggested next steps
- We can host a 60-minute technical deep-dive (Mina + infra team) to walk the access matrix and show how keys are handled in each mode.
- Karthik / legal: please accept the attached DPA redlines or propose edits; we can incorporate a 60-day subprocessor notice if Acme prefers.

Sandra — would you prefer the 60-minute deep-dive next Wednesday (June 11) or Thursday (June 12)?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
